officialSummary: The UN on Wednesday continued scaling up assistance to areas affected by the deadly earthquake that hit Colombia two days earlier.
title: UN continues scaling up response to earthquake in Colombia

officialSummary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday upheld the safety of childhood vaccines in response to a new directive from the White House to overhaul the recommended inoculation schedule.
title: WHO chief voices concern over Trump Administration’s executive order on vaccines

officialSummary: Cholera is spreading rapidly across West and Central Africa, with active outbreaks now in six countries and millions of children at growing risk, UN children’s agency UNICEF has said.
title: Cholera spreads across borders in West and Central Africa

officialSummary: A strike on a merchant ship off the southern coast of Yemen that reportedly killed several seafarers on Tuesday threatens to reignite deep concerns about global trade, amid the ongoing Iran-US war that has choked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty

officialSummary: The United Nations has once again urged warring parties in Sudan to protect civilians as the fighting continues to take a heavy toll on the population.
title: Sudan: Attacks and further displacement in Blue Nile and North Kordofan

officialSummary: Five years after the Taliban seized power, women and girls in Afghanistan have been systematically stripped of their rights, UN agencies said on Wednesday. De facto authorities have issued more than 100 decrees curbing education, work and freedom of movement – restrictions now compounded by deep cuts to aid on the ground.
title: Five years after Taliban takeover, Afghan women ‘erased from public life’

officialSummary: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms everything from how we learn, to the job market, children are adopting the technology more than three times faster than adults – exposing them to unique opportunities and risks.
title: Youth advocates gather in New York to launch new AI standards

officialSummary: Severe weather, war, economic pressure and shifting policies reshaped migration journeys across multiple regions in the first four months of 2026, driving a surge in deaths, according to new data released on Wednesday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
title: Migrant deaths climb sharply in 2026, new UN data shows
